Student projects

EPICS in IEEE

Up to US$10,000

Open · closes 1 October 2026

Student engineering teams working with community or nonprofit partners to solve local challenges. A strong starting point for assistive technology projects.

Who can apply?

Students, a community partner and at least one IEEE member must be involved. Projects should finish within one year.

Community projects

IEEE Tech4Good

US$2,500–10,000

2026 deadline passed · 15 March

IEEE volunteer teams deploying technology for sustainable development, including water, energy, education and community resilience.

Who can apply?

The primary applicant must be an IEEE Professional member or higher. An established local partnership is required.

Group activities

SIGHT Group Activity Initiative

Up to US$300

2026 deadline passed · 31 August

Small grants for SIGHT group activities, training and preparation for community projects.

Who can apply?

For active, established SIGHT groups at least 12 months old, with officer and activity reporting requirements. One application per calendar year.

Events & conferences

IEEE HTB Event Sponsorship

Up to US$2,500 / US$5,000

Applications closed

Silver and Gold sponsorship for eligible events that advance humanitarian technology and engage the IEEE humanitarian technology community.

Who can apply?

For qualifying events, rather than routine group meetings or project seed funding. Sponsorship includes programme engagement requirements.

Community enterprises

IEEE Smart Village

Project-based seed funding

Confirm current intake

Support for sustainable community enterprises connecting electricity access, education and livelihoods.

Who can apply?

Best suited to scalable community enterprises and NGOs. Applications follow a phased assessment; the programme does not list a fixed overall grant amount.

BEFORE YOU APPLY

Start with the community.

A useful proposal connects a clearly understood local need with a practical plan. Prepare these together with your community partner:

  • The challenge, who benefits and how you identified the need.
  • Your team, community partner and relevant IEEE affiliation.
  • An itemised budget, timeline and measurable outcomes.
  • A plan for maintenance, local ownership and continued use.
